sentences.text: The learned High Court Government Pleader accepts notice for the respondent No.1 - State.
2. Sri Hasan Magadi, learned counsel files power on behalf of the respondent No.2.

3. The petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 6, who are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of D V Act, are before this Court.

4. The case of the prosecution is that the accused No.1 is the husband of the respondent No.2, the accused No.2 is the mother-in-law, the accused Nos.3 and 4 are the brothers-in-law, and the accused Nos.5 and 6 are the sisters- in-law, and they subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically, and also a demand was made to bring money from the parental home.
5.

The parties are present before this Court, and they have filed an application under Section 320(2)
of Cr.PC read with Section 482 of Cr.PC for compounding the offences stating that, they have amicably settled the dispute between among themselves, and as per the terms of the settlement, the accused No.1 and the respondent No.2 have agreed to dissolve the marriage mutually, and the respondent No.2 has no objection for quashing the impugned proceeding.
NC: 2023:KHC:28659 6.
The said application is placed on record.

7. Though the offences are cognizable and non- compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that, the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves, it would be futile exercise if the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 6 are subjected to trial, since the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement.
Hence, the continuation of criminal proceeding will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceeding in CC No.15704/2022 arising out of Crime No.255/2021 pending on the file of the learned VII Addl.

Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Bangalore, is hereby quashed.
